title: Edge proxy callchain annotation microformat (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working sketch for a compact callchain annotation microformat to be carried by edge proxies / sidecars. Goal: provide provenance and routing hints to downstream inference clusters without large header bloat or full trace payloads. Must be easy to parse in C/C++ sidecars and JS edge code, and friendly for partial trust (not everything must be signed).

Constraints / design goals: 
- <= 512 bytes extra per request in the common case (ideally < 256).
- Easy to add/remove fields (forward/back compat).
- Human-readable enough for debugging but optimized for wire size.
- Can be transported as simple HTTP header(s) or as a small binary envelope when using gRPC/QUIC.
- Support per-hop annotations (eg: proxy added ttl, route decision, sampled trace id) and a compact provenance chain summary.
- Prefer ASCII-safe compact encoding (base64url for any binary payload).

High-level idea: single header Rw-Callchain with semi-colon separated key/value pairs. Value may be a compact base64url token when > simple text. A companion header Rw-Callchain-Sig (optional) holds an HMAC or signature of selected fields for integrity across untrusted networks.

Header grammar (working):
Rw-Callchain: v=1;cid=7e4f2;pc=H:mk1|P:rt=y|S:tm=170;hops=3;flags=32
- v: format version (int)
- cid: compact correlation id (hex or base62), opaque to backends
- pc: pipe-separated provenance chunks (see below)
- hops: number of processing hops recorded (small int)
- flags: bitmask for optional features (see below)

Provenance chunk syntax: <type>:<payload>
- Type single letter: H=host-proxy, P=policy-decision, S=sampled-metric, M=muted (redaction)
- Payload limited to 32-64 chars after encoding, may be key=value pairs comma-separated
- Example: H:dc=us-west,inst=proxy-3 or P:rt=cheap (routing hint)

Examples:
1) Minimal: Rw-Callchain: v=1;cid=7e4f2
2) With route and sampling: Rw-Callchain: v=1;cid=7e4f2;pc=P:rt=cheap|S:s=1;hops=1
3) Larger token (base64url part): Rw-Callchain: v=1;cid=7e4f2;pc=H:eyJpbnN0IjoicHJveHktMyIsImRjIjoidXMtZWFzdCJ9
   (where payload is JSON {"inst":"proxy-3","dc":"us-east"} base64url-encoded)

Flags (bitmask suggestion):
- 1: sampled
- 2: requires-signature
- 4: contains-binary
- 8: redacted
- 16: debug-verbose
- 32: route-optimized

Signature header: Rw-Callchain-Sig: v=1;alg=HS256;sig=<base64url>
- Signature covers selected stable fields (v, cid, pc, hops, flags) in a canonical ordering.
- Signing key: edge signing key or service account; rotate keys via KMS metadata (link to KMS ticket).
- If flags&2 set, downstream should reject if missing/invalid signature. For partial trust, some deployments can ignore signature requirement.

Binary envelope (for gRPC/QUIC): 
- Buf: first 1 byte format version, 2 bytes little-endian length of cid, cid bytes, 1 byte flags, 1 byte hops, then N provenance entries each prefixed by 1 byte type and 1 byte length. Total kept small. Encoded as base64url in header or sent as gRPC metadata-binary field.

Why not use W3C TraceContext?
- We still use traceparent for distributed tracing. This microformat focuses on provenance/routing hints and compact per-hop annotations that are too chatty for traceparent. Also need flexibility for policy hints (eg: route->cheap) that aren't trace concerns.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Exact canonicalization rules for signature: whitespace, ordering, percent-encoding? Need a reference implementation in Go and C++.
- Should CID be globally unique or just locally unique (per-customer)? If global, consider UUIDv7 short form.
- How to support redaction: when upstream marks 'muted' or redacted fields, they get replaced with M:<reason> and flags include redacted.
- Relationship to observability sampling: if trace sample is off but flags.sampled set, we still want a light-weight sample id to probe quality metrics.
- Backpressure: when header size exceeds budget, drop low-priority provenance entries and increment a 'dropped' counter in flags/metadata. Need per-proxy enforcement.

Implementation sketch (Go pseudocode):
- ParseHeader(raw string) -> map[string]string and list of prov chunks
- Normalize for signing: join(["v=...","cid=...","pc=...","hops=...","flags=..."])
- SignWithKey(k, normalized) -> base64url(sig)

Integration notes:
- Edge proxies add a provenance chunk at ingress: H:dc=us-west,inst=proxy-3,t=170 (t = processing-ms).
- Sidecars may set P:rt=cheap or P:rt=fast depending on tenant preferences and cost-tier.
- Backend routers honor P:rt hints when capacity/price tradeoffs exist; otherwise ignore.
- Console/observability: decode pc chunks and display as a small timeline next to trace/span. If sig present, show verified badge.

Debugging ergonomics:
- A CLI tool rwcc (rw callchain) to decode and pretty-print header values. Example: rwcc decode 'v=1;cid=7e4f2;pc=H:...|P:rt=cheap' -> human timeline.
- HTTP view: colorize tokens (green = verified, yellow = unsigned, red = redacted)

Backward compatibility plan:
- v=1 header as above; proxies that don't recognize simply ignore unknown pc chunk types.
- If header absent, default to empty. Do not reject requests based on absence.

Security considerations:
- Headers may cross network boundaries; avoid leaking tenant-sensitive IDs in plain text. Encourage base64url-encoded JSON for anything tenant-specific and use encryption for extremely sensitive payloads (but that increases cost/complexity).
- Use Rw-Callchain-Sig for integrity where policies require it. For signing, prefer HMAC-SHA256 for performance; allow RSA/ECDSA for cross-domain verification.

Measuring adoption / metrics to emit:
- per-proxy: avg header size, fraction requests with flags&2, signatures verified rate, dropped-provenance-count
- console: percent of traffic with route hint honored, latency delta when route-optimized used

Notes to self / next steps:
- Flesh out canonicalization tests and write a small C++ parser for envoy filter.
- Make a tiny reference impl (Go) and a compat test harness with envoy and rust-proxy.
- Draft a short RFC for platform teams and iterate.
- Add example migration guide for tenants that currently put tenant id in X-Tenant; recommend encoding in base64 JSON chunk with minimal claims: {tid, tmeta, ds} and sign if required.

Random brain dump:
- Could add a 'q' score in provenance chunk for heuristic route scoring: P:rt=cheap,q=0.43
- Would be neat if edge computed an estimated token-cost and set a cost bucket. Backend can use this as a hint for quantization selection or model variant (eg: choose 8-bit variant if cost high).

End of scratchpad.

-- Asha
